_about: Which picture a label is shown on in Browse > preview > Mockup, and how. The photos are squares: the mockup is the whole picture.
A label uses the entry named <CATEGORY>[_pH]_<pack> (_pH for acidic products; pack as 1l, 5l, 250ml, 1kg, 250g ...),
or else the entry named <CATEGORY>[_pH] whose 'packs' cover its pack ('*g' = every g and kg pack).
Failing both, a category listed in 'same_as' uses that category's picture (MO liquids come in PAM's bottles and canisters).
kind 'wrap': wrapped round the white bottle (calibrated to PAM_1l.jpg; the body is resized to the label, which is how
the 250 ml bottle is made).
kind 'panel': a label on a flat or soft surface.
area        the four corners (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left; photo px) of the surface the label is
fitted into, keeping its proportions -- a turned face is a slanted shape, and the label follows it.
area_ratio  the real width / height of that area, when the photo shows it foreshortened (default: as it looks).
curve       [top, bottom]: how far (photo px) the area's top and bottom lines dip at the middle; the label bows with them.
inset       margin left round the label, as a share of the area's height.
paper       the label paper's colour as a share of white, per R, G, B (1, 1, 1 = pure white).
shadows     opacity of the photo's shading laid over the label in Multiply (0..1).
contrast    Levels on that shading before it is laid over (1 = as photographed, 2 = shadows twice as deep).
flatten     shade only by the surface's own creases, not the light across it: the size (share of the label width)
of what counts as a crease.
highlights  opacity of the photo's highlights laid over it in Screen (0..1).
detail      how fine the shading is, as a share of the label width (smaller = sharper creases).
bulge       how much the label's edges bow out on a puffed-up surface (0.03 = slight).
falloff     how much darker the label's corners are, where that surface turns from the light (0..1).
displace    [x, y] displacement-map strength, as a share of the picture: the label bends with the folds of the
surface (used for the foil pouch).
